Zanmu Nippaku (日白 残無 Nippaku Zanmu) was the main antagonist of the Unfinished Dream of All Living Ghost incident. She was formerly a human monk before turning into an oni after falling into hell.

Zanmu Nippaku was formerly a human monk during the Sengoku Jidai period. Zanmu discarded her humanity by absorbing beast-youkai spirits. Sensing her imminent fall to Hell, Zanmu ventured there prematurely. There she transformed into an oni and ruled Hell using her intelligence and charisma. She proposed the relocation of Hell from Former Hell, creating a great amount of resentment from those that stayed behind. Currently she resides in Hell. She is said to command great admiration and respect from the dwellers of Hell.

During the events of Unfinished Dream of All Living Ghost, she uses her ability and influence to manipulate the other protagonists in order to achieve her end goal.

Zanmu is described as the perfect oni according to Suika Ibuki. She has both the strength and intelligence that an oni should be portraying, which made her a "intelligentsia". That said and although she made it for selfish reasons, she is also seen to have a sense of grace, seeking a (relatively) peaceful resolution to the beast wars and to protect Gensokyo from destruction. In this sense, she shares much in common with Reimu, feeling a sense of communality.

Zanmu is not easily upset or angered when the events are not going exactly as she wants. She frequently forgives her bumbling assistant, Hisami, showing she can work with an acceptable error range.

According to Saki, Zanmu is a popular figure in Hell. So much so that Zanmu was able to sway the oni to calm down and let her handle the beast spirits situation.

Zanmu is a crimson-eyed girl with long purple-black hair that reaches to her knees. Her hair is straight at the scalp but becomes wavy at the end. She has two short, pointed horns that are wrapped in red strings that are adorned with a single bead and numerous, smaller strings that look like hair. She wears a green T-shirt, with two coloured borders: the outer-most one is yellow while the innermost one is black lines that aren't attached. The t-shirt's neckline, shoulders, sides and sleeves all have the same rip except for the sides, which are partly sewn together with the same red strings that adorn her horns. She also wears long blue shorts that contain many of her shirt's decorations, the borders, the rips and the red strings partly sewn together on each side. The shorts also seem to be double-layered, one being white underneath the shorts. She sports dark red flip-flops.

/// Zamnu's abilities

Capable of manipulating nothingness: Zanmu has the ability to manipulate nothingness. This causes the victim to lose their desires and motivations. It can be subtle, such as distracting the victim, or outright causing them to lose their will to fight or will to continue investigating. In Unfinished Dream of All Living Ghost, she uses her ability to distract Marisa Kirisame and Sanae from the true cause of the incident. Then, she uses her ability to cause the beast spirits leaders to lose their will to fight. Finally, she uses her ability to convince Reimu to stop her investigation.

While Zanmu is able to manipulate nothingness of her victims, some appear to be less affected than others. Reimu's instincts continued to point to Zanmu as the true culprit and Reimu was not able to be manipulated to accept her plans for "resolving the incident". Similarly, she was unable to stop Mamizou Futatsuiwa from continuing her investigating into the incident. Also, due to Hisami's unpredictable masochism tendencies, Zanmu was not able to control Hisami the way she wanted.

/// Extra Information

Zanmu is basically the queen of hell, and surprisingly she is a "human" which is the main leader of hell.

entries.name: Hisami
Sumireko
entries.content:
Sumireko Usami (宇佐見 菫子 Usami Sumireko) is the main antagonist of Urban Legend in Limbo incident. She's a human from the Outside World with psychic powers (ESP). She is the first president of the Secret Sealing Club.

Sumireko has shown herself to be extremely intelligent, determined, passionate, and hubristic in equal parts. She strongly dislikes the modern society of the outside world due to being dictated by modernized corporations and is much more interested into the occult/fantasy, in the sense of actually being directly involved with it in real life. She goes so far into the occult that it can sometimes endanger her life at times. Sumireko often gets excited of the thrill of danger however.

She describes herself as having been a bit of a loner prior to her arrival in Gensokyo but ever since she started coming to Gensokyo and befriending many inhabitants from there, she considers her discovery of Gensokyo to be the best thing to have happened in her life due to the friendships she's made there. Sumireko seems to hold several contradictory opinions, although it comes off less as hypocrisy, and more as though she hasn't been able to fully make up her mind about certain subjects due to her inexperience of being a teenager. She also tends to use friendly nicknames a lot of her close friends such as Reimu and Marisa.

She also describes herself as being chuunibyou, a term usually used mockingly, with a sense of personal pride, alluding to her psychic powers and other magical abilities. In spite of that pride, she does lament that nobody in the Outside World seems to be able to understand her or her passion about the occult and Gensokyo. This may also be in part due to how highly opinionated she is, espousing her beliefs about the "phoniness" of the Outside World's dominant consumerist culture at the slightest provocation. She also dislikes drugs such as smoking and alcohol likely due to the amount of students in her hometown who would do drugs during flower viewings.

She is a strong psychic, capable of various powers associated with the occult, including but seemingly not limited to levitation, pyrokinesis, hydrokinesis, telekinesis, psychokinesis, and teleportation.

After the events of Urban Legend in Limbo, Sumireko gains the ability to travel to Gensokyo in her dreams through a doppelganger which maintains her "permanent" presence in Gensokyo and is actually also youkai-like. She is able to recall the memories of both the time spent possessing the body of her doppelganger as well as those from her "normal" life in the Outside World, allowing her to live a double-life in both worlds. When this happens, this lead to her dream soul coexisting and even sending objects and eventually humans in Gensokyo to the outer world to lessen the shock of the Great Barrier. According to Yukari, she also strengthening the the barrier as well.

Sumireko has brown eyes and shoulder-length brown hair tied in pigtails. On her head is a black fedora with a white bow along with red-framed glasses. She wears a purple plaid skirt and matching vest (resembling a jumper dress), over a long-sleeved white blouse and a black bolo tie with a clasp shaped like a "Quimbaya airplane". Along with this, she wears white socks with bows and black shoes. Sumireko generally carries Zener cards, a tablet computer marked with a hexagram on the back, a smartphone in a white case with various blue shapes on it, and a light-blue liberator. She also wears white gloves, and a black high-collared cloak with a red interior inscribed with pinkish-white runes, and a series of white lines at the bottom rim of the backside.

Her summer uniform appears nearly identical to her winter one, but with shorter and looser sleeves, no gloves, and a skull in place of the Quimbaya airplane. In Violet Detector, her hair and eyes have a dark red tone instead.

entries.name: Urban Legend in Limbo
entries.content:
Urban Legend in Limbo Incident and Sumireko Usami's Plans:

Urban Legend in Limbo revolved around the mysterious happenings in the Netherworld, specifically concerning the spread of bizarre and unsettling urban legends. These legends aren't merely stories; they manifest as tangible phenomena, capable of affecting the world and its inhabitants.

At the heart of this unsettling situation is Sumireko Usami, a human girl from the Outside World possessing powerful psychic abilities (ESP).  She isn't simply a bystander; she's the main cause of the incident, actively involved in the creation and manipulation of these urban legends.  Her motivations are complex and not entirely malicious, but her actions have far-reaching consequences.

Sumireko's primary goal wasn't world domination or outright destruction. Instead, she seeks to create a world shaped by her own unique understanding of reality.  She believes the existing world is dull and lacks the excitement and wonder found in compelling stories.  To achieve this, she uses her psychic powers to weave and spread urban legends, essentially rewriting reality to better suit her vision.  These legends act as building blocks in her grand plan to reshape the world.

Her methods involve planting seeds of unusual events and manipulating perceptions to make the legends seem more real and impactful. She wasn't directly causing harm, but the chaotic consequences of her actions create problems for others. This makes her more of a chaotic agent than a straightforward villain.

While the details of her ultimate goals remain somewhat ambiguous, it's clear that she desires a world filled with wonder and intrigue, a world where the lines between reality and fiction are blurred. Her actions, while causing problems, stem from a desire to create something more engaging and fantastical than the mundane reality she's experienced.

Adding another layer to her antics is the Secret Sealing Club (or Hifuu Club), a group she founded. They're not your typical book club; they're more like a coven of urban legend enthusiasts. They help spread her stories and add their own creative spins to them. Think of it as her team of mischievous minions, all dedicated to spreading chaos and mayhem. They are also heavily implied to be involved in the events of the game.

In short: Sumireko's not trying to conquer Gensokyo; she's trying to entertain it... in the most delightfully terrifying way possible. She's a quirky, unpredictable character whose actions are driven by curiosity, boredom, and a healthy dose of mischief. She's the ultimate Gensokyo troll, and we wouldn't have it any other way!

entries.name: Cirno
entries.content:
Cirno (チルノ Chiruno) is an ice fairy who first appeared on the second stage of Embodiment of Scarlet Devil. In comparison to other fairies, she is relatively strong; however, compared to the vast majority of Gensokyo's residents, her strength is subpar.

Cirno is a childish, confident fairy who appears to have a superiority complex. She proclaims herself to be "the strongest" on three separate occasions in Phantasmagoria of Flower View. In the game's manual, she is labeled as "9. baka" (⑨. バカ, lit. "9. Idiot").

Her superiority complex makes her say and do things that could be considered "idiotic". In Hidden Star in Four Seasons, when Cirno received power from Okina Matara and was warned that it could be too much for her body to handle, she ignored Okina and just asserted that the power was entirely her own. Okina began to suspect Cirno was intentionally playing the fool, but eventually came to the conclusion that she is just a dumb fairy. In Visionary Fairies in Shrine, Cirno faced Okina once again alongside the rest of Gensokyo's fairies; despite being very clearly outmatched, Cirno insisted that Okina was "bluffing", leading Clownpiece to wonder if she really is just an idiot.

Despite this, Cirno does have some intelligence. She can read and count, showing knowledge of rounding and fractions in Great Fairy Wars. In Phantasmagoria of Flower View's story mode, she was capable of recognizing that she was endangered in her battle against Yuuka. Additionally, when warned by Eiki Shiki that eternity does not truly exist even for fairies, Cirno solemnly reflects on her own mortality and the prospect of being sent to Hell, though Aya Shameimaru manages to talk her into focusing on enjoying the present.

Among other things, she enjoys using her abilities to freeze frogs, then watch them revive while thawing out in the water. However, about one in every three attempts, it fails, resulting in the frog being shattered into pieces.

Cirno has the ability to manipulate cold to the point of being able to freeze water. However, even while saying "manipulate", when coldness is in an omitted state, it seems like her surroundings are chilly even in summer. In battle, she uses this ability to attack others with icicles, huge ice cubes, or wieldable weapons like swords, but also to freeze her opponents or their danmaku. However, despite being able to freeze something hot like flaming danmaku, she is unable to freeze lasers.

How she exactly manipulates cold is unclear, but Reisen Udongein Inaba, in one of her quotes in Touhou Hisoutensoku, speculates that when Cirno does it, she warms up inside as a result. This would mean that she just absorbs the heat in the surroundings instead of "creating" cold from nothing.

Some of Cirno's Spellcards are: Snow Sign "Diamond Blizzard"; Freeze Sign "Perfect Freeze"
"Perfect Freeeeeeeeze!"; Hail Sign "Hailstorm"; Ice Sign "Icicle Fall".

Cirno has aqua-colored eyes and hair. She wears a blue ribbon, light pink blouse, blue jumper dress and seems to be wearing white socks. She also has icicle-shaped wings. Cirno is short like any fairy (around 145 cm tall). Cirno has pale skin.

entries.name: Misty Lake
entries.content:
The Misty Lake (霧の湖 Kiri no Mizuumi) is a large lake located at the foot of the Youkai Mountain. Many fairies and youkai alike appear to gather here, especially during the summertime, given the abundant water. The lake and its environs appear to be the home of Cirno, Daiyousei and Wakasagihime.

Commonly, when someone says "The lake" (湖 mizuumi), it usually refers to the Misty Lake. The water in the lake comes from a river originating from the Youkai Mountain. While the Scarlet Devil Mansion was on an island within Misty Lake as of Embodiment of Scarlet Devil, the mansion would be said to be on a bank next to the lake itself rather than on an island in future installments and written works. At and around noon each day, a strange mist envelops the entire lake, making it difficult to see anything (hence the origin of the name). The origin of this mist is unknown, but it appears that because of the bad visibility, the lake isn't as big as one would think – it would take about an hour to walk the full length around the river, so one can estimate the circumference to be about 3.1 miles (5 km).

Extremely large monster fish live in the lake as well, and can occasionally be caught on nights of the new moon. This has led to the lake being popular amongst anglers who aim to catch such a fish. These fish range from 2 to 5 fathoms (in essence up to 9 meters), with the largest on recording as 10 fathoms (this is believed to be an exaggeration).

A Master of the Lake also lives there. However, his house is so deep down that only fish or amphibians may dive down there.

It is said that creatures can't live in the lake, making it way more clear.

entries.name: Gaslighting
entries.content: The technique known as "Gaslighting" involves intentionally altering or rejecting reality with the aim of causing the victim to question their own memory, perception, or mental stability. This psychological manipulation can manifest through a variety of tactics, frequently employing ongoing denial, misdirection, or misleading information. The perpetrator may persistently deny events that have occurred, dismiss the target's feelings as irrational, or provide false narratives that create confusion. Over time, this relentless distortion of reality can erode the target's confidence in their own thoughts and experiences, leading them to increasingly doubt their grasp on what is true and real. Ultimately, such tactics serve to undermine the victim's sense of self and can have profound effects on their mental well-being.

entries.name: Love Bombing
entries.content: Love Bombing is overwhelming a target with excessive affection, praise, or attention to create dependency, lower defenses, or obscure ulterior motives.

entries.name: Guilt-Tripping
entries.content: The "Guilt-Tripping" method takes advantage of the target's feelings of duty or compassion by presenting requests or demands in a way that suggests fulfilling them is essential to relieve the manipulator's pain or dissatisfaction. This technique often involves the manipulator expressing their emotional distress or disappointment in a manner that evokes sympathy and a sense of responsibility in the target. Through this approach, the manipulator skillfully frames their needs as paramount, creating an emotional burden for the target, who may feel compelled to comply in order to alleviate the perceived suffering of the manipulator. This dynamic can lead to a cycle of guilt and obligation, where the target feels increasingly responsible for the emotional state of the manipulator, further reinforcing the manipulative behavior.

entries.name: Fearmongering
entries.content: Fearmongering is amplifying or fabricating threats, dangers, or consequences to provoke anxiety and coerce compliance with the manipulator’s agenda.

entries.name: Isolation
entries.content: Isolation is systematically cutting off the target from external support systems (friends, family, resources) to increase reliance on the manipulator.

entries.name: Moving the Goalposts
entries.content: Moving the Goalposts continuously changing expectations, criteria, or demands to ensure the target cannot meet them, perpetuating control or dissatisfaction.

entries.name: Scarcity Tactic
entries.content: Scarcity Tactic is creating artificial urgency or exclusivity (e.g., “limited time,” “only for you”) to pressure quick decisions without rational evaluation.

entries.name: Projection
entries.content: Projection technique is accusing others of behaviors, motives, or flaws that the manipulator themselves exhibits, deflecting accountability.

entries.name: Triangulation
entries.content: Triangulation technique is introducing a third party (real or imagined) to create jealousy, competition, or insecurity, destabilizing the target’s confidence.

entries.name: Emotional Blackmail
entries.content: Emotional Blackmail technique is threatening to harm oneself, others, or the relationship unless the target complies with demands.

entries.name: Shaming
entries.content: Shaming technique is attacking the target’s self-worth through humiliation, ridicule, or public embarrassment to enforce compliance or silence dissent.

entries.name: Silent Treatment
entries.content: Silent Treatment technique is withholding communication or affection to punish non-compliance, induce anxiety, or force concessions.

entries.name: Negging
entries.content: Delivering backhanded compliments or subtle insults to undermine the target’s confidence and increase susceptibility to influence.

entries.name: Bait-and-Switch
entries.content: Bait-and-Switch technique is luring the target with an appealing offer or promise, then substituting it with a less desirable outcome after commitment is secured.

entries.name: Mirroring
entries.content: Mirroring technique is mimicking the target’s behaviors, values, or speech patterns to foster false rapport and trust.

entries.name: Victim-Playing
entries.content: The "Victim-Playing" strategy involves creating or amplifying personal struggles to gain sympathy from others, shift blame away from oneself, or rationalize excessive demands that may not be reasonable or justified. This technique often manifests in various contexts, where individuals may present themselves as perpetual victims of circumstance, thereby manipulating those around them to elicit a sense of compassion or obligation. By portraying their situations in an exaggerated or fabricated manner, they aim to foster an environment where their demands are met with understanding and compliance, regardless of the validity of their claims.

entries.name: Coercion
entries.content: Coercion technique is using overt threats, intimidation, or force to compel action, often framed as unavoidable consequences of non-compliance.

entries.name: Love Withdrawal
entries.content: Love Withdrawal technique is removing affection, approval, or connection as punishment for disobedience, reinforcing conditional acceptance.

entries.name: Flattery
entries.content: Flattery technique is doing excessive, insincere praise to lower the target’s critical judgment and create indebtedness.

entries.name: Feigned Ignorance
entries.content: Feigned Ignorance technique is pretending confusion, forgetfulness, or misunderstanding to avoid responsibility, derail conversations, or gaslight.

entries.name: Divide and Conquer
entries.content: Divide and Conquer technique os creating or exacerbating conflicts between individuals or groups to prevent unified resistance and consolidate power.

entries.name: Exploiting Insecurities
entries.content: The "Insecurities-Exploit" strategy focuses on the identified weaknesses of an individual, such as their looks, intellect, or previous traumatic experiences, with the aim of diminishing their self-worth and enhancing their susceptibility.

Urine Tests: Most common and can be done at home. You simply urinate on a test stick or collect urine in a cup and dip the test.
